title: Critical Connections in a Network
spaceBreakdown:
- adj (adjacency list): 2m ints → O(n + m)
- disc: n ints → O(n)
- low: n ints → O(n)
- stk (explicit DFS frames): up to n frames → O(n)
- not counted: input connections, returned res
approach: A connection is critical exactly when it is a bridge: no alternate path connects its endpoints, i.e., it lies on no cycle. Tarjan's bridge algorithm computes, during one DFS, a discovery time `disc[u]` and a `low[u]` value (the earliest discovery time reachable from `u`'s subtree using at most one back edge). Edge `(parent, u)` is a bridge iff `low[u] > disc[parent]`. I implement the DFS iteratively with an explicit frame stack so a skewed 10^5-node path cannot overflow the call stack.
hints: For an edge to be safely removable, what kind of alternate route must exist between its two endpoints? The constraints allow up to 10^5 servers and 10^5 connections, so checking each edge by deleting it and re-running connectivity is too slow.

Use Tarjan's bridge algorithm: one DFS tracking `disc` (entry time) and `low` (earliest entry time reachable from the subtree). In Example 1, node 3 has no back edge, so `low[3]` stays at its discovery time 4 while `disc[1]` is 2; since `low[3] > disc[1]`, edge (1,3) is a bridge.

**Smallest input** - only two servers and one link, nothing else to route through.
`Input: n=2, connections=[[0,1]]` → `Expected: [[0,1]]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the bridge check for nodes with a single neighbor → returns `[]`

**Pure cycle** - every edge lies on a cycle, so none is critical.
`Input: n=3, connections=[[0,1],[1,2],[2,0]]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: using `low[v] >= disc[u]` (articulation-point test) instead of `low[v] > disc[u]` → returns `[[0,1]]`

**Skewed path** - a line of 10^5 nodes, every edge is a bridge and the DFS goes 10^5 deep.
`Input: n=100000, connections=[[0,1],[1,2],...,[99998,99999]]` → `Expected: all 99999 edges`
⚠️ Bug: recursive DFS → stack overflow / segfault on the deepest path

**Star graph** - one center, all leaves; every spoke is a bridge.
`Input: n=4, connections=[[0,1],[0,2],[0,3]]` → `Expected: [[0,1],[0,2],[0,3]]`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `low[u]` to 0 instead of `disc[u]` → `low[leaf]=0 ≤ disc[center]`, returns `[]`

followUps.q: Find articulation points (critical servers) instead of critical connections.
followUps.a: Reuse the same DFS. A non-root node u is an articulation point if it has a child v with `low[v] >= disc[u]`; the root is one iff it has at least two DFS children. Time stays O(n + m), space O(n + m).

followUps.q: Connections are added and removed online; after each operation report whether the graph is still 2-edge-connected.
followUps.a: Build the bridge-tree (compress each 2-edge-connected component into one node; bridges become tree edges). A dynamic-tree structure (link-cut tree) maintains connectivity under edge updates in O(log n) per operation, versus O(n + m) per re-run.

followUps.q: Group servers into 2-edge-connected components (servers that stay mutually reachable after any single edge removal).
followUps.a: Run the same Tarjan pass; whenever `low[v] > disc[u]`, that edge separates components. Assign component IDs by a second DFS that does not cross bridge edges, or label during the first pass. Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).
